title: Hot Honey Soppressata Pizza
seoTitle: Hot Honey Soppressata Pizza | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Sweet heat, charred salami
description: Sweet heat, charred salami. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Hot Honey Soppressata Pizza in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch pork. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Simmer quick pizza sauce
steps.instruction: Simmer crushed tomatoes with garlic and oregano 12 minutes until slightly thick. Cool 5 minutes — hot sauce on raw dough makes a wet center.

steps.title: Preheat stone to 500°F
steps.instruction: Heat stone or steel at 500°F at least 40 minutes. Tear mozzarella and slice soppressata thin — thick coins curl and shield the cheese from browning.

steps.title: Stretch rounds and sauce lightly
steps.instruction: Stretch dough to 12–14 inches with a defined rim. Sauce in a thin layer; leave the rim clean for blistering. Brush rims with olive oil.

steps.title: Cheese and soppressata
steps.instruction: Layer fresh and shredded mozzarella, then soppressata in an even shingle pattern — gaps mean bare bites, piles mean greasy pools. A light dusting of parmesan is optional before the bake.

steps.title: Bake until salami edges curl
steps.instruction: Bake 10–13 minutes until cheese bubbles and soppressata edges crisp and cup slightly. Rotate for even color. Hot Honey Soppressata needs char on the meat, not pale pink disks.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F with a 3-minute rest. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Hot Honey Soppressata Pizza onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Hot honey drizzle and cut
steps.instruction: Rest 2 minutes. Drizzle hot honey in thin zigzags and hit with a pinch of red pepper flakes. Cut into 8 slices per pie. Sweet heat hits after the bake — honey burns if added too early.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Hot Honey Soppressata Pizza — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Cut pies into hall slices (8 per pie minimum) and fan on sheet trays.
Keep a fresh pie warming in the oven — pizza dies fast on the counter.
Line up Hot Honey Soppressata Pizza on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Sweet heat, charred salami. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Hot Honey Soppressata Pizza runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
